intro: Now you write it. The sentence starter is the same one on your Make the Case page — use it. Getting used to it now is how it becomes automatic in June, when every point on the Regents essay counts.
prompt: Name the principle from the card on page 2, and say what this document does to it.
sentence_starter: This case is about ________. The documents show it being (upheld / denied / fought over) because ________.
checklist: Names the principle by its card name
Says whether the document upholds it, denies it, or fights over it
Points to the words that show it
model_response: This case is about Natural Rights — every person is born with rights that government exists to protect. Document 6 shows it being denied, because the Cherokee say they have “a perfect and original right” to their land and are being “deprived of our national and individual rights.”
_turned_in: The kid pastes it into BONUS · 11.3A Gauge Run on Google Classroom by hand. The Arena sends nothing.
source_document: Document 6 — General Council of the Cherokee Nation, address to the people of the United States, New Echota, July 17, 1830
source_text:
. . . We are not willing to remove; and if we could be brought to this extremity [last step], it would be not by argument, not because our judgment was satisfied, not because our condition will be improved; but only because we cannot endure to be deprived of our national and individual rights and subjected to a process of intolerable oppression.
We wish to remain on the land of our fathers. We have a perfect and original right to claim without interruption or molestation [being bothered]. The treaties with us, and laws of the United States made in pursuance of treaties, guaranty our residence, and our privileges and secure us against intruders. Our only request is that these treaties may be fulfilled, and these laws executed. . . .
